title: RMS Language Definition
description: Every RMS command, its attributes, preprocessor directives, and runtime control keywords, for DE — section membership, argument shapes, mutual exclusivity. Powers the parser, Monaco autocomplete/highlighting (src/editor/aoe2RmsLanguage.ts's COMMANDS/ATTRIBUTES lists should eventually be generated from this file instead of hand-duplicated), and Breakdown's command/attribute dropdowns. Attributes are defined once in the top-level attributes[] array and referenced by name from each command that accepts them, rather than duplicated per command — a command's own attributes[] field is just a list of names pointing into that array.

sections.description: The section headers a script is divided into (e.g. <PLAYER_SETUP>), in generation order. Written without the angle brackets here.

predefinedLabels.description: Condition labels the engine defines itself, usable as the ConditionLabel of if/elseif without any #define (random_map.def is the authoritative in-engine source; transcribed here from the guide's Conditionals section and Map Sizes table). Two consumers, one array: validate()'s unknown-constant check treats these as defined, and the preview generator (docs/preview-design.md Sec.3.1) builds its branch-selection environment by choosing which of these are true for the current generation settings. Do not duplicate this list in code.

name.description: Note the pattern admits a leading digit: 4_PLAYER_GAME and 2_TEAM_GAME are real engine labels (docs/parser-design.md Sec.13).

category.description: What decides whether this label is true. The preview generator switches on this to build its environment: mapSize reads the map-size setting, playerCount the player-count setting, gameVersion is always DE, and the team categories are undefined until a teams setting exists.

dimensions.description: mapSize labels only: the map's side length in tiles. The legacy and modern names are offset by one size for Normal/Large/Huge (LARGE_MAP and MAPSIZE_NORMAL are both 200), which is why this is data rather than something a consumer derives from the name — see docs/preview-design.md Sec.4. Area-based scaling is computed as dim squared over 10000; the guide's rounded area-ratio column is deliberately not stored.

mapSize.description: mapSize labels only, and only where the app offers that size: the matching MAP_SIZES value in src/generationSettings/generationSettingsConstants.ts. Absent on sizes reachable only via the MORE_MAP_SIZES launch option or override_map_size, which no setting can select but a script may still branch on.

optional.description: Whether this trailing argument may be omitted. Schema action item (docs/parser-design.md Sec.13); honored by the parser if present.

variadic.description: Whether this trailing argument may repeat. Schema action item; honored by the parser if present.

cautionBelow.description: If set, values below this threshold are still valid RMS (unlike min, which is a hard documented floor) but carry a real risk worth flagging live (e.g. a negative border value that can crash the game if it pushes the land origin off-map). Requires cautionMessage.

cautionMessage.description: User-facing warning shown (live diagnostic RMS0217, and in hover) when a value trips cautionBelow. Should explicitly say the value is valid RMS, not an error, then explain the risk and the recommended mitigation.

acceptsKnownName.description: Suppresses the known-name half of the Sec.6 stop set for this slot only, so a command or attribute name written here is consumed as the value instead of ending the argument list. Set it only where a known name is the POINT rather than a mangled line — today that is #const's value slot alone, because Sec.2.1 lets a script alias any name and `#const restricted_terrain_distance max_distance_to_other_zones` is correct RMS. Not derivable from `type`: 15 other otherConstant slots exist and on those a known name really is a mistake worth stopping on.

section.description: One of the top-level sections[] entries, e.g. "LAND_GENERATION". This records where the GUIDE DOCUMENTS the command, which is not the same as where the engine accepts one — see sectionLocked. Never enforce a diagnostic off this field alone.

sectionLocked.description: True only when the engine has been MEASURED to discard this command outside its `section`. Drives validate()'s RMS0304 (docs/parser-design.md Sec.10); absent means unknown and RMS0304 reports nothing, which is the default for all but the measured few. It is a separate field from `section` on purpose: `section` is a documentation fact and this is an engine fact, and enforcing the former as if it were the latter warned 53 times on the corpus with 52 of those on shipped working maps (`effect_amount` outside <PLAYER_SETUP>), the false-positive class BUG-002 and BUG-005 already cost this project three rounds. Set it only alongside a `notes` entry naming the run that measured it.

tokenId.description: The engine's own internal token id for this command name, and ONLY when a run has measured it. Per docs/parser-design.md Sec.2.1 the engine resolves every word to one integer and constants share that space with commands, so a script writing `#const L 32` makes `L` indistinguishable from the command holding id 32. Drives the parser's alias resolution; absent means unknown and a `#const` to that value resolves to nothing, which is the default for all but the measured few. Same species of field as `sectionLocked` and same discipline: it is an ENGINE fact, never transcribed from a map author's comment, and it is set only alongside a `notes` entry naming the run. Sibling of `constId` in game-constants.json, which records the same integer space for constants.

kind.description: block = opens a { } body (e.g. create_land { ... }). standalone = a single statement with inline arguments and no body (e.g. base_terrain GRASS).

arguments.description: Inline arguments taken by this command itself (both kinds can have these — a block command's MaxHeight-style argument, or a standalone command's whole argument list).

attributes.description: Names of entries in the top-level attributes[] array valid inside this command's { } block. Only meaningful when kind is "block"; omit or leave empty for standalone commands.

deprecated.description: Present when the engine still accepts this command but a patch has superseded it. The string is the user-facing replacement guidance, shown verbatim by validate()'s RMS0309 (docs/parser-design.md Sec.8). Cite the patch that obsoleted it in notes.

mutexWith.description: Names of other attributes that cannot be used together with this one in the same block, e.g. land_percent vs. number_of_tiles.

mutexNote.description: What the guide says actually HAPPENS when this attribute and a mutexWith partner appear in one block, plus the guide's own advice. Appended to RMS0307's message when present. Only set it where the guide states the consequence: for most pairs it says 'mutually exclusive' and nothing more, and the generic message says exactly that much.

repeatable.description: Whether this attribute is cumulative (multiple instances in one block are all applied), e.g. replace_terrain. Governs whether Breakdown offers an 'add another' affordance — not whether duplicate instances render as a list; that's the ground-truth rule (docs/breakdown-design.md Sec.3.3, source presence, not this flag).

maxRepeats.description: Caps the 'add another' affordance for a repeatable attribute. Do not add without re-checking DE patch notes (Update 153015) per docs/parser-design.md Sec.8. None is sourced today.

requiresOneOf.description: Attribute names, at least one of which must appear in the SAME block for this attribute to do anything. Transcribes a guide 'Requires:' line, and the failure is silent: ignore_terrain_restrictions without set_place_for_every_player or place_on_specific_land_id makes the whole create_object place nothing at all (guide:2509, confirmed in game 2026-08-10 on AK_Namatjira.rms). validate() raises RMS0315. Set it only where the guide states the requirement AND the consequence is known, the same bar requiresSection carries.

requiresNote.description: What actually happens when a requiresOneOf requirement is unmet, in the author's terms. Appended to RMS0315's message. Sibling of mutexNote and set for the same reason: the consequence differs per attribute and belongs in the data, not in a name check inside validate.ts.

requiresSection.description: A top-level sections[] name that must be present somewhere in the script for this attribute to do anything. validate() raises RMS0311 when the attribute is used and the section is absent. The only entry today is base_elevation, which needs <ELEVATION_GENERATION>: without it the map still generates and looks correct, but the slopes never take effect. Set this only for engine-verified cases — it is the one error-severity semantic check.

nonFunctional.description: True for names the DE exe carries as strings with no behaviour behind them (the guide's Non-Functional Syntax appendix: min_distance, max_distance, set_position, percent_of_land). Same meaning as the directive flag. validate() raises RMS0310 rather than letting the parser report a bare unknown name.

replacedBy.description: Name of the working attribute this dead string corresponds to, rendered into RMS0310's message. Distinct from a deprecation: a deprecated command still works, these never did. Only meaningful alongside nonFunctional.

nonFunctional.description: True for directives the DE exe accepts but that do nothing at runtime (#undefine/#include — engine ghosts, parser-design.md Sec.7/Sec.13). Drives Breakdown's 'has no effect in DE' badge (Sec.3.6).

commands.name: create_land
commands.description: Creates a land mass on the map.

attributes.name: land_percent

arguments.name: percent
arguments.description: Share of the map this land should occupy.

attributes.description: Sets land size as a percentage of total map area, instead of an absolute tile count.

directives.name: #const
directives.description: Defines a named integer constant usable anywhere a number is expected.

controlKeywords.name: start_random
controlKeywords.description: Begins a block of percent_chance-weighted alternatives, closed by end_random.
